transcript: Walden is a new play at Second Stage about a pair of sisters reuniting after one was in space and the other has moved to a remote cabin with her partner. Set in the maybe not-too-distant future, humanity is grappling with whether or not to double down on potential space habitation or do what we can to save our dying planet. It's science fiction but it's a very vivid story with a compelling premise coupled with well-formed characters who all have rich backstories. What I appreciated the most about this play was that it's relevant and thought-provoking by means of simply great storytelling. In other words, the themes aren't too in-your-face which is a common issue I find with topical pieces. This play, though topical, still is rooted in emotional and dramatic stakes. It moves really nicely and really clips by at a swift 90 minutes thanks to solid writing, performances, and direction. Walden is running at the Tony Kaiser Theater through November 24th. With that, other playwill for my collection.
